zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the puzzle, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When outputting the solution grid, ensure each value matches the original wording.
zebralogic.example: Changing 'Blue Master' to 'blue master' or 'BlueMaster', altering case or spacing.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says 'X is directly left/right of Y', enforce that the house numbers differ by exactly one in the specified direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains the phrase 'directly left of' or 'directly right of'.
zebralogic.example: Placing X two houses away from Y when the clue says X is directly left of Y.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says 'X is somewhere to the left/right of Y', enforce a strict ordering (X < Y or X > Y) without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains 'somewhere to the left/right of' or similar ordering language.
zebralogic.example: Allowing X to be to the right of Y when the clue says X is somewhere to the left of Y.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., 'the person who loves pop music is the person who loves romance books'), link those values across categories.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses 'is the person who' or 'is the same as' to connect two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'pop music' and 'romance books' as unrelated when a clue says they belong to the same person.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., 'the person who loves science fiction books is in house 5'), place that attribute in that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue explicitly mentions a house number for an attribute.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the science‑fiction book to a house other than house 5 despite the clue.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Before final output, ensure the JSON object is syntactically valid: proper brackets, commas, quotes, and correct ordering of keys.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response, before submitting the answer.
zebralogic.example: Missing a closing bracket or using single quotes instead of double quotes.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with any reasoning before it, so the verifier extracts the answer correctly.
zebralogic.example: Appending extra commentary after the JSON, causing the verifier to miss the answer.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B, B = C), propagate the links so all linked attributes are unified.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When there are several clues that connect attributes indirectly.
zebralogic.example: Failing to deduce that X = Z when X = Y and Y = Z.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between two entities, enforce that the absolute difference in their house numbers is N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions 'N houses between' or 'N houses apart' with a specific number.
zebralogic.example: Treating '2 houses between' as a difference of 2 instead of 3.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that a particular attribute value is not in a specific house (e.g., 'X is not in house N'), enforce that the attribute cannot be assigned to that house; without this, the solver may place the value there, violating the clue.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a negation about a house position, such as 'not in the third house', 'cannot be house 2', or 'never in house 5'.
zebralogic.example: Placing the 'blends' smoker in house 3 despite the clue 'The person who smokes many unique blends is not in the third house'.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting "N houses between" as "N houses apart" (using a difference of N instead of N+1).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the phrase as a direct distance, forgetting that 'between' implies there must be N houses separating the two, resulting in a difference of N+1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When parsing such clues, add one to the given number to compute the house index difference.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to generate explanatory text after the JSON, leading the verifier to stop parsing early or miss the JSON entirely.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Terminate all reasoning before outputting the JSON and ensure no characters follow the closing bracket.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the final answer to be truncated.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model generates too much reasoning, exceeding the output token limit, resulting in the JSON being cut off.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise, use length control, and prioritize the final JSON.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model overlooks or misinterprets negation in clues, treating 'not in house N' as irrelevant, leading to assignments that violate the clue.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue contains a negation about a house, explicitly mark that attribute as prohibited from that house and enforce the exclusion.
